normalization.overview: Matt Pocock proposes one versioned home repository containing shared agent skills, steering, a wiki and tools, with paths to separately owned code repositories. Source-first analysis weighs navigation benefits against ownership and permission boundaries.
normalization.whyItMatters: Organizations working across multiple repositories often duplicate instruction files and agent skills. A shared discovery surface can simplify navigation, but centralizing knowledge and connected tools also concentrates operational context and access pathways.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: Treat the home repo as a shared map and knowledge layer, not a monorepo or authorization system. Pilot one cross-repo workflow; preserve destination-level permissions, owners, CI and release controls.
normalization.falsification: Compare the same authorized two-repo task from the existing launch setup and a read-only home index, tracking correct repo discovery, stale guidance, changed file scope, reviewer effort and owner interventions.
normalization.freshness: November 12 creator video and creator article; original-media ReasonPack verified; machine captions not independently listening-certified; Git and harness docs support mechanisms but not measured outcome improvement.
